name: Creatine monohydrate

lead: Creatine monohydrate is the most widely studied sports supplement. Creatine itself is a nitrogen-containing compound made in the body from amino acids and also obtained from meat and fish; the monohydrate salt is the standard supplemental form. It is sold as a low-cost, flavourless powder.

In physique and performance circles it is used to support strength, lean mass gain during resistance training and repeated high-intensity effort. Many randomized trials and position stands report modest but consistent gains in these outcomes, and the wiki's evidence rating for it is strong.

paras: Muscle stores creatine mostly as phosphocreatine, which rapidly regenerates ATP during short, intense efforts. Supplementation raises intramuscular creatine content, which researchers say can allow slightly more training work to be done and may encourage greater adaptation over time. Part of the early scale-weight increase is attributed to water drawn into muscle cells.

Creatine is legal and sold over the counter. Reviews of long-term use in healthy people have found it generally well tolerated, with water retention and occasional gastrointestinal upset the most commonly reported complaints. It can modestly raise serum creatinine without necessarily reflecting kidney damage, which can complicate lab interpretation, and people with kidney disease are advised to seek medical advice first. Responses vary and some people are reported as non-responders.
